verdict.rationale: Nix is a package manager and declarative system builder, not a workflow-automation tool. Its documented model still maps onto part of this story. Configurations are declared as code in configuration.nix or flakes. Upgrades are atomic and add new versions rather than overwriting old ones. Users can roll back with `nix-env --rollback` or restore an entire NixOS system configuration to an earlier state. The 'review' element is not evidenced, and versioning of 'automations' is only implied through declarative config and coexisting package versions. Missing for 10: an explicit review/diff workflow for changes, evidence of versioning automations specifically (as opposed to packages and system configs), and independent hands-on corroboration of rollback in practice.
